title: Omega-3 and DHA in Pregnancy: Food Sources and Supplement Cautions
excerpt: Why DHA matters for fetal development, low-mercury fish options, and when to ask a clinician about supplements
content:
## Introduction to Omega-3 and DHA
Omega-3 and DHA are two types of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) that are crucial for the health of both mother and fetus. DHA (Docosahexaenoic acid) is a type of omega-3 fatty acid that is particularly important for the development of the fetus's brain and vision.

## Role of DHA in Pregnancy
DHA plays a critical role in supporting the development of the fetus's brain and vision. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), DHA also helps reduce the risk of preterm birth and mental health problems in children.

## Food Sources of Omega-3 and DHA
Food sources rich in omega-3 and DHA include:
- Salmon
- Sardines
- Anchovies
- Alaskan salmon
- Nuts and seeds such as walnuts and flaxseeds

## Mercury in Fish
When consuming fish, it's essential to be aware of the mercury levels in the fish. According to the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), it's recommended to limit consumption of fish with high mercury levels such as shark, swordfish, and king mackerel.

## Omega-3 and DHA Supplements
If you're pregnant and considering taking omega-3 and DHA supplements, it's crucial to consult with your healthcare provider before taking any supplements. According to the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), it's recommended to choose supplements that contain DHA and are manufactured by reputable companies.

## Conclusion
Omega-3 and DHA are essential fatty acids for the health of both mother and fetus. To ensure adequate intake of these fatty acids, it's recommended to consume food sources rich in omega-3 and DHA and consult with your healthcare provider before taking any supplements.
